attributes.description: A synthetic reel. One invented story. Listen to Ember Tide Protocol.

products.merchandising_summary: When the tide engines of a drowned moon fall silent, one stubborn engineer has a single night to wake them – and an even stranger night to survive.
products.publisher_summary:
A SYNTHETIC SUMMARY WRITTEN FOR MECHANICAL LIBRARIAN TESTS.

Winner of no award at all

Nell Arvane keeps the tide engines of Kessa, a moon that is mostly sea, turning through the long dark.

When the engines stop and the harbour begins to freeze, she has until dawn to learn why – with only a borrowed lantern and a radio that answers in riddles.

The engines were built by a dozen rival guilds, none of which wrote anything down, and the only manual is a song the harbour children sing badly. Nell knows three verses. The fourth, the one that matters, was lost when the old lighthouse keeper moved inland to grow turnips.

So she sets out across the ice in a flat-bottomed boat with a cat who refuses to be useful, a thermos of lukewarm tea and a growing suspicion that the engines did not stop by accident.

Along the way she meets a cartographer who maps only coastlines that have not formed yet, a choir of buoys that hum in a minor key, and a rival engineer who insists on doing everything in the wrong order and is, annoyingly, sometimes right.

By the time the sky begins to pale, Nell has learned the fourth verse, lost the cat twice, and discovered that a moon can hold a grudge – and that the tide will only turn if somebody asks it nicely.

Meanwhile, back in the harbour, the mayor holds an emergency meeting about the ice, the fishmongers hold a louder one about the mayor, and the lighthouse keeper's turnips win a prize nobody expected. None of this helps Nell in the slightest, but all of it is written down, at length, because a real publisher's summary is long and this invented one has to be long too, so that the documents a test builds from it weigh what the real ones weigh.

Part puzzle, part voyage, Ember Tide Protocol is a story invented to exercise a parser, not to be read.

PLEASE NOTE: This text is fictional and describes no real recording.

One minute. Then one hour. Then one year.

Every morning at 6:14 Tobin Reyl slips a little further ahead of the world he knows, and his daughter starts building a clock to catch him.

products.publisher_summary:
Quando Nell Arvane si sveglia, le maree di Kessa sono ferme e il porto comincia a gelare. Né la radio né la lanterna sanno dirle perché: ha soltanto una notte per capirlo.

A bordo della Brace, Nell è sola. O forse no?

Le macchine delle maree furono costruite da dodici corporazioni rivali, e nessuna scrisse mai un manuale: resta soltanto una canzone che i bambini del porto cantano male. Nell ne conosce tre strofe; la quarta, quella che conta, è andata perduta.

Attraversa il ghiaccio con una barca a fondo piatto, un gatto che si rifiuta di rendersi utile e il sospetto crescente che le macchine non si siano fermate per caso.

Un riassunto inventato per i test, con accenti: è, à, ù, ò.
